name: The Decency Press
link: the Decency League's pamphlet printers out front, the toy factory behind.

areas.name: The Reading Room
areas.what: the shopfront: pamphlets, a counter, a League volunteer

areas.name: The Print Floor
areas.what: presses, paper rolls, drying racks overhead

areas.name: The Line
areas.what: the toy assembly line: conveyors, stamps, a paint shop, a testing booth

areas.name: The Loading Yard
areas.what: vans, a weighbridge, a gatehouse with dogs

areas.name: The Boiler House and chimney
areas.what: the furnace and a 60 m chimney with a ladder

areas.name: The Foundry
areas.what: the furnace's floor, under the chimney

shortcuts: a paper chute from the Print Floor down to the Yard
a gantry from the Line across to the Boiler House

keys.name: Rivet's test: get a lure to land in a bin from across the Yard
keys.joke: Rivet scores her out of ten. She gives six. "I'm generous."

keys.name: The Reading Room: command the volunteer to fetch the "trade catalogue"
keys.joke: It has two covers. The inner one's the toy catalogue.

keys.name: The drying racks: cross the Print Floor on the racks while pamphlets dry on them
keys.joke: Nim comes out with DECENCY printed backwards on her side.

keys.name: The proof copy: the next pamphlet's proof is in the press; swap it
keys.joke: The swapped proof prints Swyne's photo upside down. Six thousand copies.

keys.name: The magpie: cross the whole Line without quality control looking up
keys.joke: The magpie's caught a lure. He's keeping it.

keys.name: The weighbridge: a van's overloaded; Open its back with its driver's own hands
keys.joke: Nim tells him to weigh himself next. He does.

keys.name: The chimney: climb all 60 m, then come down head first
keys.joke: Vesper's not at the top. A note is: "Proud of you. Don't fall."

keys.name: The guard dogs: through the Yard and out the far gate with every dog still asleep
keys.joke: One dog wakes, sees her, and goes back to sleep. Professional courtesy.

keys.name: Five testers woken
keys.joke: They give the product one star, all five of them.

contraband: 100 contraband (toys off the line, crates in the vans)
tin: the League's collection tin in the Reading Room
people_in_trances: five testers who tried the products, still sitting in the testing booth. Nobody hurts them.
enemies: Goons: moles in overalls and goggles, who work the line and fight. They're poor-sighted, so lures work twice as well on them.
Guard dogs in the Yard: Dobermans on chains, with handlers. They smell her. Lures, or the roofs.
Quality control: a magpie on a high stool over the line, who watches for anything out of place. Doesn't fight, pulls the line's alarm.

set_piece.name: The line, backwards
set_piece.summary: Rivet's plan: run the whole line in reverse, so it unmakes what it made.
beats: Nim fights through the Line to the control room and throws the switch.
The conveyors run backwards and pick up speed. She rides them upstream, through the stamps, the paint shop, the testing booth, jumping between belts as presses come down in reverse.
The magpie pulls the alarm. Goons come down the belts toward her. She lures them off the sides.
At the end of the line, everything that's been made goes back in as raw parts.
set_piece.punchline: the line's last trick, run backwards, is to reprint the Reading Room's pamphlets as blank paper.

boss.name: Foreman Grubb
boss.summary: A mole in a giant press of his own design, the Decency Engine: a printing press on legs. He fights in the Foundry.
phases: The plates. The Engine stamps the floor in patterns. Nim reads the pattern, and the lures make him stamp the wrong way.
The ink. He floods the floor with ink, and she can't stay on it. She climbs the walls and swings across the ceiling chains with the rope.
The feed. She drops down into the Engine's feed and, from inside, the crop jams the rollers.
boss.punchline: the Engine, jammed, prints its last sheet: Grubb's signed confession, which he'd written in case anyone asked. Bound to the press. Nobody's printing anything tonight.

leaves_with: The lures, and the knowledge she can do it alone.
The broadcast schedule: midnight, City Hall's clock tower, the night of the vote. And the gift bags for the Ball.
Back at the club, Vesper's home from the hearing. She doesn't talk about it. She asks how the chimney was.
owner_review: Every joke in the Key table, the names Foreman Grubb and the Decency Engine, Vesper's note, and Rivet's lines. The hearing on the radio (Swyne's lines).
story: Coming in: the Retreat's order forms come from the Decency Press, the League's printers in the industrial quarter. Rivet has a schematic of the building already. She drew it from memory after a tour. "They gave me a pamphlet. I gave them nothing."

The same night: Vesper is called before the Council's Decency Committee. She goes, in her coat, calm. Nim hears it on the radio as she works: Swyne names "a certain club in the Old Quarter" in public, and Vesper doesn't deny it. The bell tower in this world is empty.
The Press: a red-brick works with a chimney. Out front, a reading room full of pamphlets: DECENCY: A GUIDE FOR THE FAMILY. Behind it, the line, making toys.

Going out: the foreman's office holds the broadcast schedule: midnight, City Hall's clock tower, the night of the Decency Act vote. And an order for six hundred gift bags for the Council's Decency Ball.
how_it_teaches: Nothing new from Vesper. Rivet's lures after her test (Key 1): throw a seized toy, it buzzes, and guards go to look. A world built to use everything together, with the lures as the extra.
notes: The factory. It leans covert, and it's the first world where Vesper isn't watching.
No new lesson: Vesper has taught everything. This world tests it.
The map: a factory in four halls, with a yard and a chimney.
